sections.title: Context
sections.body: The British Council is a global organisation promoting English language learning and cultural exchange. This project involved redesigning their digital learning platform to reach learners across India and other emerging markets at scale, and building a teacher collaboration platform to support their global educator network.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: The existing digital learning offer was not reaching the volume or breadth of learners the British Council needed to serve. Engagement on existing platforms was low, and teachers had no shared digital infrastructure for collaboration across markets. The business problem was scale: extending reach without proportionally increasing cost.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I led the product and design work, including user research, platform design, and the teacher collaboration tool. Delivery was a joint effort with the engineering team; product and UX decisions were mine.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: User research focused on the specific constraints of learners in emerging markets: device availability, connectivity, and the role of the teacher in a learner's experience. The platform was designed around low-bandwidth usage patterns and teacher-led learning pathways. The teacher collaboration platform was built to allow educators across markets to share lesson materials, adapt content, and coordinate programmes without central coordination overhead.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body:
• 3M+ active learners on the platform
  • 40% engagement uplift
  • Teacher collaboration platform deployed across multiple countries including India
